body:
### Summary

uv follows a repository-controlled `.ok` symlink when marking a Git checkout
ready. A Git dependency can track `.ok` as a symlink to an existing writable
file outside the checkout. During a successful `uv pip install`, uv follows
that symlink and truncates the target. Native Git clone plus `git reset --hard`
leaves the target unchanged.

There is no error: the installation succeeds. Reproduce with:

```sh
unzip attachments.zip
cd attachments
UV_BIN=uv ./reproduce.sh uv-git-ok-repro
```

Relevant output:

```text
uv_version=uv 0.12.17 (7f9bce21f 2026-09-20 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
uv_source_revision=7f9bce21fbcb00c2799c402afb5411e1ed614f9e
tracked_ok_kind=120000
native_clone_rc=0
native_reset_rc=0
native_external_unchanged=yes
install_rc=0
victim_after_bytes=0
external_marker_consumed=yes
package_build_consumed=yes
```

The Git source controls `.ok` as a symlink to a pre-existing victim file. The
native-Git control does not alter the victim, while uv's checkout marker write
does. The detailed source analysis, impact, exact revisions, and reproduction
materials are in `report.md` and `attachments.zip`.

**Attachments**

[report.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32436141/report.md)

[attachments.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32436143/attachments.zip)

### Platform

Linux 6.1.0-53-cloud-amd64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.12.13 (`0ebbd9274a55a8a53a13970be3b97e4209598e17`); also reproduced on current main, uv 0.12.17 (`7f9bce21fbcb00c2799c402afb5411e1ed614f9e`).

### Python version

Python 3.11.2
title: uv Git checkout marker follows a repository-controlled symlink
